scenario.fault_family: link cut (both fabric uplinks of one leaf)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
A user on pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) reports a total outage: nothing across the
fabric responds, and pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) cannot reach pc_0_1 either.
pc_0_1 CAN still ping its own gateway 10.0.1.1, and leaf_router_0_1
itself is up and reachable on its console -- its FRR daemons are all
running. Both of its BGP sessions to the spines are gone. Diagnose.

ip link set eth0 down
  ip link set eth1 down

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth0 | grep -c UP
ip -br link show eth1 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_1 eth0 and eth1 -- BOTH fabric
  uplinks: eth0 (172.16.0.7/31, link subnet 172.16.0.6/31) to
  spine_router_0_0 and eth1 (172.16.0.11/31, link subnet
  172.16.0.10/31) to spine_router_0_1
Mechanism: leaf_router_0_1's only paths into the CLOS fabric are its
  two spine uplinks. With both interfaces down, both BGP sessions drop
  and the leaf can neither learn 10.0.0.0/24 nor deliver its own
  10.0.1.0/24 traffic anywhere -- the CLOS redundancy is defeated
  because BOTH members of the redundant pair are down. The host-facing
  port eth2 (10.0.1.1/24) is untouched, so pc_0_1 still reaches its
  gateway but nothing beyond it. Note this is the one link-fault shape
  where redundancy does not save the leaf; a single downed uplink
  would only degrade redundancy.
Localization: leaf_router_0_1
Root cause: both spine-facing interfaces (eth0, eth1) down on
  leaf_router_0_1
Fix: `ip link set eth0 up` and `ip link set eth1 up` on
  leaf_router_0_1; both BGP sessions re-establish on their own.
scenario.fix_spec:
`ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up` on leaf_router_0_1. Once
the uplinks are UP the sessions to both spines come back and pc_0_1
regains fabric reachability.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** Both uplink interfaces on leaf_router_0_1 — `eth0` (the link to spine_router_0_0 via 172.16.0.7/31) and `eth1` (the link to spine_router_0_1 via 172.16.0.11/31) — are administratively DOWN (`<BROADCAST,MULTICAST>`, no `UP` or `LOWER_UP` flags). The access interface `eth2` toward pc_0_1 remains up, which is why local gateway reachability is preserved.

**Mechanism:** With both uplinks down, FRR's bgpd cannot complete a TCP connection to either spine peer. Both BGP neighbors transitioned to `Active` state (attempting connection) and were reset ~3-4 minutes ago with reason "No path to specified Neighbor (n/a)" — the FRR reset code triggered when the next-hop interface disappears from the kernel. With zero BGP sessions established, leaf_router_0_1 holds no BGP-learned routes; its entire routing table is reduced to `10.0.1.0/24 dev eth2`. Any packet from pc_0_1 destined for a cross-fabric address (e.g. 10.0.0.2) hits the gateway, finds no matching route, and is returned as ICMP Destination Net Unreachable. pc_0_0 times out symmetrically because no path back to 10.0.1.0/24 exists via that router.

**Localization:** leaf_router_0_1, interfaces eth0 and eth1. Spine sides (spine_router_0_0:eth2 and spine_router_0_1:eth2) are both UP, confirming the fault is leaf-local.

**Root cause:** Both uplink interfaces (eth0, eth1) on leaf_router_0_1 were brought down, severing all fabric connectivity and collapsing its BGP sessions.

**Fix:** Bring both interfaces back up on leaf_router_0_1: `ip link set eth0 up && ip link set eth1 up`. BGP will re-establish automatically within the connect-retry interval (120 s), restore learned routes, and restore full pc_0_0 ↔ pc_0_1 reachability.

The writeup's inferences follow logically from those observations and include the correct remediation.
